title: Private upgrades GA requirements (supported paths, rollback guarantees, docs, success metrics)
creator: Vivek Kulkarni
description:
Goal
Define and align on GA requirements for Redwood Private (VPC + on-prem/air-gapped) upgrades with deterministic rollback entry points. This ticket is the source of truth for: supported upgrade paths, rollback guarantees, documentation requirements, release gating, and success metrics.

Background / why now
Private customers are asking for clear rollback guarantees and auditable upgrade artifacts. We have multiple parallel workstreams (installer plan generation + prechecks + backup/restore + rollback hooks + compatibility gating + Helm ordering + Terraform pinning) and need a crisp GA bar to avoid scope creep while ensuring operator safety.

GA scope (what we will claim for GA)
1) Supported upgrade paths
- Default supported path: N-1 -> N for the Redwood Private platform version (in-place upgrade).
- Patch upgrades within same minor: N.x.y -> N.x.z supported.
- N-2 (or older) -> N upgrades: NOT GA-guaranteed. Tooling should detect and block or require explicit override with “manual intervention required” guidance.
- Installer version compatibility: installer must support upgrading Private platform versions within the published compatibility matrix; tool should warn when installer is older than recommended.

2) Rollback guarantees (what we promise)
- Operator-invoked rollback is supported for the same N-1 -> N window, with deterministic rollback entry points.
- Rollback will restore the last known-good control-plane + configuration state recorded at upgrade start, and will verify post-rollback health checks.
- Rollback is best-effort for data plane workloads; we will document the expected behavior for in-flight inference requests (e.g., brief interruptions, reconnect required for streaming clients) and any known non-reversible changes.
- DB/schema: GA guarantee is “safe by default” migrations with guardrails (idempotency, lock timeouts) and defined rollback semantics. Where down-migrations are not supported, the upgrade plan must fail earlier (before irreversible step) OR require explicit operator acknowledgement.

3) Operator UX requirements (installer)
- Commands must be stable and documented:
  - redwood-private upgrade plan (generate plan + compatibility evaluation)
  - redwood-private upgrade precheck (run preflight checks only)
  - redwood-private upgrade apply (execute plan)
  - redwood-private upgrade status (current stage/step + pointers to logs)
  - redwood-private rollback (consume stored upgrade state + execute rollback hooks)
- Output must be actionable: each precheck failure includes severity (block/warn), exact failing condition, and remediation steps.
- Plan and execution artifacts must be persisted locally and in the cluster (so support bundles can capture them).

4) Documentation / customer-facing guidance (GA minimum)
- “How to upgrade Redwood Private” guide (VPC + on-prem differences called out).
- Precheck catalog with remediation.
- Backup and restore guidance including encryption expectations and retention.
- Rollback procedure and when to choose rollback vs manual remediation.
- Troubleshooting section for the top failure modes (artifact verification failures, insufficient storage headroom, DB migration lock timeout, Helm hook/job timeouts, OIDC/RBAC reachability).
- Change management template: maintenance window guidance, comms checklist, and post-upgrade verification.

5) Release gating and approval requirements
- GA requires:
  - Compatibility policy enforced (block unsupported paths by default).
  - Prechecks enforced with clear block vs warn thresholds.
  - Backup completes successfully (or explicit operator override with audit event + warning).
  - E2E upgrade tests for at least one VPC scenario and one on-prem/air-gapped scenario per release train.
  - Release Eng + SRE sign-off for each Private GA release candidate.

6) Auditability / compliance
- Audit log events emitted for: upgrade started, prechecks pass/fail, backup started/completed, apply started/completed, rollback invoked/completed.
- Audit events include: actor, environment identifier, from_version, to_version, installer_version, plan_id, result, and timestamps.
- Support bundle contains: last plan JSON, execution log, precheck results, backup verification results, rollback log (if used).

Non-goals for GA (explicitly out of scope)
- Fully automated multi-hop upgrades across multiple major versions.
- Automatic resolution for every historical schema edge case (must provide clear “manual intervention required” guidance).
- Always-on blue/green upgrades for Private.

GA success metrics (targets we will track)
- Upgrade success rate (N-1 -> N) >= 98% across beta + first 30 days GA (success = apply completes + post-upgrade verification passes without human intervention beyond documented prompts).
- Rollback success rate >= 95% when invoked from supported rollback entry points.
- Median time to recover (MTTR) from upgrade-related incidents <= 60 minutes (includes rollback execution time).
- Reduction in upgrade-related support tickets by 30% vs prior quarter baseline (normalize by number of active Private environments).
- Precheck block reasons distribution is measurable; top 3 categories have documented remediation and are referenced in installer messaging.

Open questions / decisions needed before GA
- Define “irreversible step” line for DB migrations per release (and make plan generator fail before it unless explicit acknowledgement is set).
- Decide whether backups are hard-blocking for all GA environments, or block-by-default with a break-glass override (requires Security/Compliance alignment).
- Confirm minimum k8s versions and storage backends in the GA support statement (tie to integration test matrix).

acceptance_criteria: GA requirements are reviewed and approved by Product (Vivek), Release Eng (Connor), SRE (Sean), and Security (Naomi) with any exceptions explicitly documented.
Supported upgrade paths are documented (including explicit non-goals) and map to compatibility enforcement in tooling.
Rollback guarantees are stated in operator-friendly language with a clear definition of supported rollback points and known limitations.
Docs checklist is complete with owners assigned for any remaining gaps (upgrade guide, prechecks/remediation, backup/restore, rollback, troubleshooting, change-management template).
Success metrics are defined with measurable targets and an owner for reporting (dashboards or weekly report).
Release gating checklist exists and is referenced by the Private release train notes (sign-off + required evidence).
metrics: Rollback success rate (when invoked from supported points): >= 95%
Upgrade-related support tickets: -30% QoQ (normalized by # of active Private environments)
Precheck block rate breakdown available by category (storage, DB, RBAC/OIDC, TLS/DNS, artifacts)
rollout_plan: Beta: PM-826 design partners (1 VPC, 1 on-prem/air-gapped) complete at least one N-1 -> N upgrade + rollback drill in a maintenance window.
GA readiness review: confirm docs, gating evidence, and audit events; finalize external-facing wording for rollback guarantees.
GA launch: enable as default workflow for new Private releases; Support playbook updated; incident-bot tagging and dashboards validated.
Post-GA 30-day review: metrics readout + backlog for N-2 support and additional automation based on top precheck blockers.
comments: 2025-05-06 (Talia Benson): Drafted GA bar v0.1 based on kickoff notes + recent support escalations. Flagged open question: should backup be hard-blocking or break-glass with audit event?

2025-05-14 (Vivek Kulkarni): Aligning with Markus/Fatima: on-prem partner requires offline bundle verification + explicit rollback steps that don’t assume external registry access. Added doc requirements for air-gapped flow.

2025-05-22 (Connor O’Brien): From Release Eng POV, GA must include a defined test matrix per release train (at least 1 VPC + 1 on-prem). If we can’t run on-prem nightly, we need a per-RC gating job before cutting GA artifacts.

2025-06-03 (Naomi Feldman): Security review note: break-glass backup override is acceptable only if (a) explicitly acknowledged in CLI, (b) emits audit event with reason, and (c) docs state it may limit rollback guarantees.

2025-06-11 (Sean Gallagher): SRE request: define what “success” means operationally (health checks + error rate window). Also want MTTR metric to include time-to-rollback completion when rollback is recommended.
